task_summary: Implement a TypeScript/React Home Page component featuring a closed-loop SVG diagram (circular layout of tool nodes) and a quick-start table. The component consumes ToolDef data, transforms it into DiagramNode and QuickStartRow structures, computes circular layout positions, and renders an interactive SVG diagram plus a quick-start section. All within a Vite+React 18+Tailwind CSS v3 stack using Convex for data.

findings.finding: The standard approach for placing N nodes in a circle uses: x = centerX + radius * cos(2π * i / N - π/2), y = centerY + radius * sin(2π * i / N - π/2). The -π/2 offset places node 0 at the 12 o'clock position. This is a pure geometric computation with no library dependency needed. The computeNodePosition function should accept a 0-based or 1-based step index, totalNodes, centerX, centerY, and radius, returning {x, y}. Edge cases: totalNodes=0 (guard against division by zero), totalNodes=1 (single node at top).
findings.source: Standard computational geometry / D3.js radial layout conventions
findings.relevance: Directly implements computeNodePosition and the circular diagram layout

findings.finding: Use a viewBox attribute (e.g., '0 0 500 500') on the SVG element to make diagrams responsive. Combine with preserveAspectRatio='xMidYMid meet' and set width/height via Tailwind classes (w-full, max-w-lg, etc.). This avoids hardcoded pixel dimensions and ensures the diagram scales cleanly across breakpoints. The SVGViewBoxSpec type should encode minX, minY, width, height.
findings.source: MDN SVG viewBox documentation, responsive SVG patterns
findings.relevance: Critical for making ClosedLoopDiagram responsive within Tailwind layout

findings.finding: SVG elements in React use camelCase attributes (strokeWidth, fillOpacity, etc.). Text centering inside SVG uses textAnchor='middle' and dominantBaseline='central'. For connecting nodes in a closed loop, draw lines or paths between consecutive nodes and from the last node back to the first. Use <g> groups for each node (circle + text) to simplify transforms. Avoid inline styles; use Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax or SVG presentation attributes directly.
findings.source: React documentation on SVG, common open-source diagram components

findings.finding: The mapper functions (toQuickStartRow, toDiagramNode) should be pure functions with explicit return types. Use Array.map for the list variants (toQuickStartRows, toDiagramNodes) — these are trivial wrappers. Keep transformations in a separate utility file or co-located with the component but exported for testability. The ToolDef likely contains fields like slug, name, color, description, steps; the mappers extract/reshape relevant subsets.
findings.source: Functional programming patterns in TypeScript/React codebases
findings.relevance: Defines the data flow architecture from tool_data through transformations to rendered components

findings.finding: Given the 300-line file limit, the Home Page should be split: (1) HomePage.tsx — top-level layout, (2) ClosedLoopDiagram.tsx — SVG diagram component, (3) homeTransforms.ts — pure transformation functions (toQuickStartRow, toDiagramNode, compute*). This keeps each file focused and testable. The HomePage component orchestrates data fetching (potentially via Convex useQuery), applies transforms, and renders sub-components.
findings.source: Project operating procedures, React component architecture best practices
findings.relevance: Ensures compliance with the 300-line limit and separation of concerns

findings.finding: If ToolDef data comes from Convex, use useQuery from 'convex/react' to fetch it reactively. Handle the loading state (useQuery returns undefined while loading). If tool data is static/hardcoded (from a tool_data module), no Convex query is needed — just import directly. The dependency on 'tool_data' suggests the latter: static data imported as a TypeScript module.
findings.relevance: Determines whether data flow is static import or reactive query

findings.finding: For a closed-loop (cycle) diagram, edges connect node[i] to node[(i+1) % N]. Render edges as SVG <line> or <path> elements BEFORE nodes so nodes render on top (SVG painter's model — later elements occlude earlier ones). For directional flow, add arrowhead markers via <defs><marker>. To prevent arrows from overlapping node circles, shorten line endpoints by the node radius using vector math: dx = x2-x1, dy = y2-y1, len = sqrt(dx²+dy²), offset = nodeRadius/len, then adjusted endpoints are (x1+dx*offset, y1+dy*offset) → (x2-dx*offset, y2-dy*offset).
findings.source: SVG marker specification, graph visualization best practices
findings.relevance: Core rendering logic for the closed-loop diagram arrows/edges

findings.finding: Add role='img' and an aria-label to the top-level <svg> element. Include a <title> element as the first child of <svg> for screen readers. For interactive nodes, use role='button' and tabIndex on <g> elements if clickable. Ensure sufficient color contrast for node labels against node fill colors.
findings.relevance: Ensures the diagram is accessible; commonly overlooked in SVG components

findings.finding: The type StepNumber (primitive) likely represents a 1-based step ordinal displayed to users. The computeNodePosition function should handle conversion internally: if StepNumber is 1-based, subtract 1 before applying the angle formula. This is a common off-by-one pitfall in circular layout code.
findings.source: Convention analysis from type naming; common layout bugs
findings.relevance: Prevents off-by-one positioning errors in the circular layout

findings.finding: For a small number of nodes (typical tool count is likely <20), no virtualization or memoization is necessary. However, wrapping transform functions with useMemo keyed on the tools array prevents unnecessary recomputation on re-renders. The SVG diagram with <20 nodes has negligible rendering cost. Avoid re-creating arrow marker definitions on each render — define them once in a <defs> block.
findings.source: React performance documentation, SVG rendering benchmarks
findings.relevance: Ensures no premature optimization while following basic memoization hygiene

recommended_approach:
Split implementation into three files:

1. **src/components/home/homeTransforms.ts** (~80 lines) — Pure transformation functions:
   - `toQuickStartRow(tool: ToolDef): QuickStartRow`
   - `toDiagramNode(tool: ToolDef): DiagramNode`
   - `toQuickStartRows(tools: ToolDefList): QuickStartRowList` (maps over array)
   - `toDiagramNodes(tools: ToolDefList): DiagramNodeList` (maps over array)
   - `computeNodePosition(step: StepNumber, totalNodes: number, centerX: number, centerY: number, radius: number): CircularLayoutPoint` — uses trigonometric formula with -π/2 offset for 12-o'clock start; converts 1-based StepNumber to 0-based index internally.

2. **src/components/home/ClosedLoopDiagram.tsx** (~120 lines) — SVG diagram component:
   - Accepts `ClosedLoopDiagramProps` containing `DiagramNodeList`.
   - Defines SVGViewBoxSpec constant (e.g., 0 0 500 500).
   - Calls `computeNodePosition` for each node.
   - Renders `<svg>` with `<defs>` for arrowhead marker, `<line>` edges forming a closed loop (with endpoint shortening for arrow clearance), and `<g>` groups for each node (circle + label text).
   - Uses Tailwind for outer container sizing (w-full, max-w-xl, mx-auto).
   - Includes aria-label and `<title>` for accessibility.

3. **src/pages/HomePage.tsx** (~100 lines) — Page component:
   - Imports static tool data from `tool_data` dependency.
   - Applies `toDiagramNodes` and `toQuickStartRows` transforms (memoized with useMemo).
   - Renders hero section with heading/description, `<ClosedLoopDiagram>` component, and a quick-start section displaying QuickStartRows in a responsive grid/list using Tailwind.
   - Exports `HomePage` as default for React Router integration.

All types (QuickStartRow, DiagramNode, CircularLayoutPoint, SVGViewBoxSpec, etc.) are imported from the `type_registry` dependency. Tool data is imported from `tool_data`. No external diagram libraries needed.
alternatives_considered: Use a third-party diagram library (e.g., react-flow, d3-force) — rejected because the layout is a simple fixed circle with known node count; a library adds unnecessary bundle weight and complexity for this use case.

Render the diagram using HTML/CSS (absolute positioning + border-radius) instead of SVG — rejected because SVG provides native support for lines, arrows, viewBox scaling, and is semantically appropriate for diagrams.
Put all logic in a single HomePage.tsx file — rejected due to the 300-line limit and testability concerns; splitting into HomePage.tsx, ClosedLoopDiagram.tsx, and homeTransforms.ts is cleaner.
Use CSS Grid or Flexbox for the quick-start table — viable and preferred over an HTML <table> for responsive design with Tailwind utility classes.
Fetch tool data from Convex at runtime vs static import — the dependency on 'tool_data' module suggests static data; using a static import avoids loading states and simplifies the component.
risks: Off-by-one error in StepNumber if it is 1-based but used as 0-based index in angle computation — mitigate by explicit conversion in computeNodePosition.
SVG arrow markers not rendering correctly across browsers if marker-end syntax or refX/refY values are wrong — mitigate by testing in Chrome, Firefox, Safari.
Division by zero if totalNodes is 0 in computeNodePosition — guard with early return or default.

Type mismatches between ToolDef fields and expected DiagramNode/QuickStartRow fields if type_registry and tool_data modules have not yet been implemented — mitigate by defining clear interfaces and using the type_registry dependency.
Circular layout may look poor at extreme aspect ratios or very small viewports — mitigate with responsive viewBox and sensible min-width constraints.
HexColor values from ToolDef may not meet WCAG contrast requirements against white text — mitigate by using darker fills or adding a contrasting stroke/background.
compliance_notes: All files use .ts or .tsx extensions — no Python.
All exported functions and components have explicit TypeScript type annotations.
React functional components only; no class components.
Props typed with TypeScript interfaces (imported from type_registry).
Tailwind CSS classes used exclusively; no custom CSS.
Bun is the package manager; no npm/yarn/npx commands.
Each file stays under 300 lines per the file size preference.
React hooks (useState, useEffect, useMemo) used for state management.
Convex hooks would be imported from 'convex/react' if needed; current design uses static imports so no Convex queries required for this component.
Component must be routable via React Router v6 — HomePage exported for route configuration.
